$comment: Boundary / hostile / unusual values. `documentedStatus` is what the CURRENT build returns (verified by the API suite); `expectedStatus` is what a hardened API should return. Mismatches are tracked as bugs — see harness/bugs/known-issues.md.

submissions.notes: Record is stored with score=undefined and never appears in any leaderboard.
String is stored verbatim and breaks numeric ordering in the leaderboard.
In-memory mode stores the object; a MongoDB deployment rejects it at the Mongoose cast layer.
The client only ever produces integers (one point per apple).
No server-side plausibility check exists — a forged client can top the board (covered by TC-119/TC-119b).
The UI blocks this (playerName.trim() === ''), the API does not.
UI caps input at 20 chars ([a-zA-Z0-9 ]); the API has no limit and the name is echoed back in leaderboard payloads.
Stored raw. React escapes it on render, so it is a stored-data hygiene issue, not a live XSS.
No trimming happens, so '  Padded  ' and 'Padded' become two separate players.
UI input filter keeps only [a-zA-Z0-9 ], so unicode can only arrive through the API.

submissions.case: name that is a foul-word substring (false positive)
submissions.notes: Foul filter uses String.includes() on the lower-cased name, so 'cock' matches inside 'hancock'.
Every blocked name collapses into the single player 'Anonymous', so unrelated runs merge and overwrite each other.

submissions.case: concurrent submissions of the same name
submissions.notes: In-memory mode is single threaded. The MongoDB path does findOne + save without an atomic upsert and can create duplicate documents — UNKNOWN / REQUIRES VALIDATION, tracked as BUG-018 (TC-135).
